output: injection_timing_factor_cyl3_b = Q12 multiplier (4096 = 1.0) for the L029 angle injection_timing_factor_cyl3_a; injection_timing_demand_cyl3 = a x b / 4096 is one candidate in the main injection timing selection (injection_timing_select_mode_cal: 0 sum, 1 max, else min; it is 1 here) that ends in torque_limit_fault_snapshot (main injection timing)

output: injection_timing_demand, assigned directly (source_priority 5) only while cold_start_phase is CSP_ABOVE_RPM_TRIGGER (2), CSP_ABOVE_RPM_VIA_EVENTS (6) or CSP_SETPOINT_UNDERRUN (7): engine rpm above engine_rpm_trigger_cal but below governor_rpm_setpoint_output (or fallen back below it after reaching it); then copied to torque_limit_fault_snapshot (main injection timing), or offset by injection_timing_offset_cal + DAT_0005a48a and clamped +/-1024 in injection_delivery_mode 3
units_check: x 0..7200 = 0..900 rpm (the start run-up range); y -1920..14080 = -30..220 F (signed, flags 6); grid 119..222 = 13.9..26.0 deg at 0.1171875 deg per count, 24..26 deg at -30 F falling to 14..15 deg at 220 F
evidence: The call sits in the cold_start_phase branch that skips the four component tables, its result is the whole main timing for that branch, and the values are advanced when cold and about 15 deg hot. torque_limit_fault_snapshot is sent in PGN 65504 at x 120 / 1024 deg per count and is the main timing the auxiliary offset is measured from.
naming_concern: Named by behavior, not by the cold_start_phase vocabulary: that phase machine (mpc555_processColdStartMainLoop) has no coolant condition and steps CRANKING -> ABOVE_RPM_TRIGGER at engine_rpm_trigger_cal -> AT_GOVERNOR_SETPOINT at governor_rpm_setpoint_output on every start, so cold start is a legacy name for the engine start / run-up machine (the table covers -30..220 F). Cranking (phase 1) uses the component path instead. Cache word torque_limit_init_state_0 is a misnomer.
